Based on the provided context, the Commission may designate a general-purpose AI model as presenting systemic risks on the basis of criteria set out in Annex XIII, which include:
- The number of parameters of the model
- The quality or size of the data set (for example measured through tokens)
- Biological sequences (as indicated in Annex XIII)
- The benchmarks and evaluations of capabilities of the model (including the number of tasks without additional training, adaptability to learn new tasks, level of autonomy and scalability, and tools it has access to)
- Whether it has a high impact on the internal market due to its reach (presumed when made available to at least 10,000 registered business users established in the Union)
- The number of registered end-users
- Having high impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators and benchmarks
- Having capabilities or an impact equivalent to high impact capabilities based on a decision of the Commission, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel

Regarding whether the provider can challenge it:
Yes. A provider can present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, the model does not present systemic risks and therefore should not be classified as such. Furthermore, upon a reasoned request containing objective, detailed, and new reasons (which can be made at the earliest six months after the designation decision, or six months after a decision following a reassessment), the Commission may reassess whether the model can still be considered to present systemic risks.
reason: The assistant accurately identified the Annex XIII criteria and the challenge/reassessment procedures mentioned in the context and reference answer, with all claims fully supported by the text.
